name: Prohibition on the Purchase of Residential Property by Non-Canadians Act — scope, exemptions and end date
description: Federal ban on non-Canadians buying residential property (up to three dwelling units, including condominium units) located in a census metropolitan area or census agglomeration. In force since 1 January 2023; scheduled to end on 1 January 2027 after the 2024 two-year extension. Whether the user may buy depends on immigration status, which is unknown (USER-PROFILE.md).

attributes.end_date_basis: Two-year extension announced 4 February 2024 (Department of Finance); repeal provision S.C. 2022, c. 10, s. 236 shown as not yet in force on the Justice Laws consolidation current to 2026-09-30.
attributes.extension_beyond_2027_status: No official extension, repeal or replacement found as of 2026-10-30; secondary sources (September–October 2026) report a federal review but no announcement.
attributes.who_is_non_canadian: An individual who is not a Canadian citizen, a person registered under the Indian Act, or a permanent resident; foreign-incorporated corporations; certain Canadian private corporations controlled by non-Canadians; prescribed persons (Act s. 2).
attributes.property_covered: Buildings with up to three dwelling units and parts of buildings such as semi-detached houses and condominium units; buildings of four or more units are not covered; vacant land excluded since 2023-03-27.
attributes.geographic_scope: Only property inside a census metropolitan area (CMA) or census agglomeration (CA); purchases outside CMAs/CAs are not prohibited.

exemptions.status: Canadian citizen, permanent resident, person registered under the Indian Act
exemptions.rule: Not a non-Canadian; the Act does not apply.

exemptions.status: Temporary resident holding a work permit or work authorization
exemptions.rule: Exempt if at least 183 days of validity remain on the permit or authorization on the purchase date and the person has not already bought residential property in Canada during the prohibition.

Exempt only if enrolled in an authorized program at a designated learning institution, filed Canadian tax returns for each of the 5 preceding years, physically present at least 244 days in each of those 5 years, purchase price not over $500,000, and no prior purchase during the prohibition.

exemptions.status: Protected person / person granted refugee protection
Refugee claimant whose claim was referred to the Refugee Protection Division, or temporary resident under a humanitarian public policy
Spouse or common-law partner of a citizen, permanent resident, registered Indian or exempt non-Canadian, buying together
Accredited diplomat / member of a foreign mission

exemptions.rule: Acquisition through divorce, separation, gift or death; creditor enforcing security; purchase for development; section 35 Indigenous and treaty rights; publicly traded corporations not covered. Renting a home is not a purchase.

attributes.penalty: Fine up to $10,000 on summary conviction for the buyer and anyone who knowingly helps; a superior court may order the property sold, with the non-Canadian receiving no more than the price paid.

limitations: The regulations (SOR/2022-250) contain the detailed conditions; read them before any purchase. Status two months before expiry: an extension, lapse or replacement framework may be announced at any time — re-check before 2027-01-01. Provincial taxes on foreign buyers (BC, ON, NS) are separate and do not expire with this Act.
